elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 12.4 now reads "Customer is subject to no non-compete or field-of-use restriction under this Agreement.", replacing the prior 24-month worldwide prohibition on developing, marketing, selling, or acquiring any competing product or service. Retained § 12.3 reinforces that nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service or conducting business in any field or territory, and that Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. No residual field-of-use or territory limit binding Customer remains.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no restriction on Customer survives, so there is no scope to narrow to a named product. The outcome is strictly stronger than the fallback.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the post-term ("and for twenty-four months thereafter") language was deleted and no restriction of any duration remains.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the 24-month tail is gone and no restrictive period exists at all.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no prohibition on development remains, and § 12.3 affirmatively confirms Customer may develop any product or service.
Condition does not apply: the express bar on acquiring competing products was removed, and § 12.3 confirms Customer may acquire any product or service.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative sentence eliminates the non-compete rather than merely promising removal in the comment, and the deterministic check confirming no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains is borne out in substance.
Fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because there is no surviving restriction whose scope, term, duration, or carve-outs could be assessed; the preferred outcome subsumes them.

Minimal: the edit is confined to the offending second § 12.4 and substitutes a single confirming sentence; no favourable existing language (including § 12.3 and the separate no-hire covenant in the first § 12.4) is disturbed, and no survival tail, expense, remedy, or procedural extras are added.

Preserves intent: the replacement removes the direct contradiction with § 12.3 rather than creating one, leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and does not touch pricing, term, remedies, or other allocation mechanics.

No repair required; the claimed 'deviation' classification and preferred-level target are correct because the original clause was walk-away (24-month post-term, undefined 'any product or service that competes with Vendor', worldwide).
